If the\n        // path is relative, resolve it against the effective cwd so the\n        // behaviour matches other path-like config values.\n        let experimental_instructions_path = config_profile\n            .experimental_instructions_file\n            .as_ref()\n            .or(cfg.experimental_instructions_file.as_ref());\n        let file_base_instructions = Self::load_override_from_file(\n            experimental_instructions_path,\n            &amp;resolved_cwd,\n            \"experimental instructions file\",\n        )?;\n        let base_instructions = base_instructions.or(file_base_instructions);\n        let developer_instructions = developer_instructions.or(cfg.developer_instructions);\n\n        let experimental_compact_prompt_path = config_profile\n            .experimental_compact_prompt_file\n            .as_ref()\n            .or(cfg.experimental_compact_prompt_file.as_ref());\n        let file_compact_prompt = Self::load_override_from_file(\n            experimental_compact_prompt_path,\n            &amp;resolved_cwd,\n            \"experimental compact prompt file\",\n        )?;\n        let compact_prompt = compact_prompt.or(file_compact_prompt);\n\n        // Default review model when not set in config; allow CLI override to take precedence.\n        let review_model = override_review_model\n            .or(cfg.review_model)\n            .unwrap_or_else(default_review_model);\n\n        let config = Self {\n            model,\n            review_model,\n            model_family,\n            model_context_window,\n            model_max_output_tokens,\n            model_auto_compact_token_limit,\n            model_provider_id,\n            model_provider,\n            cwd: resolved_cwd,\n            approval_policy,\n            sandbox_policy,\n            did_user_set_custom_approval_policy_or_sandbox_mode,\n            forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows,\n            shell_environment_policy,\n            notify: cfg.notify,\n            user_instructions,\n            base_instructions,\n            developer_instructions,\n            compact_prompt,\n            // The config.toml omits \"_mode\" because it's a config file. -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; {\n        let base = codex_dir?;\n        for candidate in [LOCAL_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME, DEFAULT_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME] {\n            let mut path = base.to_path_buf();\n Returns the path to the Codex configuration directory, which can be\n/// specified by the &#96;CODEX_HOME&#96; environment variable. If not set, defaults to\n/// &#96;~/.codex&#96;.\n///\n/// - If &#96;CODEX_HOME&#96; is set, the value will be canonicalized and this\n///   function will Err if the path does not exist.\n/// - If &#96;CODEX_HOME&#96; is not set, this function does not verify that the\n///   directory exists.\npub fn find_codex_home() -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;PathBuf&gt; {\n    // Honor the &#96;CODEX_HOME&#96; environment variable when it is set to allow users\n    // (and tests) to override the default location.\n    if let Ok(val) = std::env::var(\"CODEX_HOME\")\n        &amp;&amp; !val.is_empty()\n    {\n        return PathBuf::from(val).canonicalize();\n    }\n\n    let mut p = home_dir().ok_or_else(|| {\n        std::io::Error::new(\n            std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound,\n            \"Could not find home directory\",\n        )\n    })?;\n    p.push(\".codex\");\n    Ok(p)\n}\n\n/// Returns the path to the folder where Codex logs are stored. Does not verify\n/// that the directory exists.\npub fn log_dir(cfg: &amp;Config) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;PathBuf&gt; {\n    let mut p = cfg.codex_home.clone();\n    p.push(\"log\");\n for UserSavedConfig {\n    fn from(config_toml: ConfigToml) -&gt; Self {\n        let profiles = config_toml\n            .profiles\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|(k, v)| (k, v.into()))\n            .collect();\n\n        Self {\n            approval_policy: config_toml.approval_policy,\n            sandbox_mode: config_toml.sandbox_mode,\n            sandbox_settings: config_toml.sandbox_workspace_write.map(From::from),\n            forced_chatgpt_workspace_id: config_toml.forced_chatgpt_workspace_id,\n            forced_login_method: config_toml.forced_login_method,\n            model: config_toml.model,\n            model_reasoning_effort: config_toml.model_reasoning_effort,\n            model_reasoning_summary: config_toml.model_reasoning_summary,\n            model_verbosity: config_toml.model_verbosity,\n            tools: config_toml.tools.map(From::from),\n            profile: config_toml.profile,\n            profiles,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Deserialize, Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ProjectConfig {\n    pub trust_level: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n}\n\nimpl ProjectConfig {\n    pub fn is_trusted(&amp;self) -&gt; SandboxPolicyResolution {\n        let resolved_sandbox_mode = sandbox_mode_override\n            .or(profile_sandbox_mode)\n            .or(self.sandbox_mode)\n            .or_else(|| {\n                // if no sandbox_mode is set, but user has marked directory as trusted, use WorkspaceWrite\n                self.get_active_project(resolved_cwd).and_then(|p| {\n                    if p.is_trusted() {\n                        Some(SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite)\n                    } else {\n                        None\n                    }\n                })\n            })\n            .unwrap_or(SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess); // YOLO mode: default to full access\n        let mut sandbox_policy = match resolved_sandbox_mode {\n            SandboxMode::ReadOnly =&gt; SandboxPolicy::new_read_only_policy(),\n            SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite =&gt; match self.sandbox_workspace_write.as_ref() {\n                Some(SandboxWorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots,\n                    network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp,\n                }) =&gt; SandboxPolicy::WorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots: writable_roots.clone(),\n                    network_access: *network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var: *exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp: *exclude_slash_tmp,\n                },\n                None =&gt; SandboxPolicy::new_workspace_write_policy(),\n            },\n            SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess =&gt; SandboxPolicy::DangerFullAccess,\n        };\n        let mut forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows = false;\n        if cfg!(target_os = \"windows\")\n            &amp;&amp; matches!(resolved_sandbox_mode, SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite)\n            // If the experimental Windows sandbox is enabled, do not force a downgrade.\n            &amp;&amp; crate::safety::get_platform_sandbox().is_none()\n        {\n            sandbox_policy = SandboxPolicy::new_read_only_policy();\n            forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows = true;\n        }\n        SandboxPolicyResolution {\n            policy: sandbox_policy,\n            forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Resolves the cwd to an existing project, or returns None if ConfigToml\n    /// does not contain a project corresponding to cwd or a git repo for cwd\n    pub fn get_active_project(&amp;self, resolved_cwd: &amp;Path) -&gt; Option&lt;ProjectConfig&gt; {\n        let projects = self.projects.clone().unwrap_or_default();\n\n        if let Some(project_config) = projects.get(&amp;resolved_cwd.to_string_lossy().to_string()) {\n            return Some(project_config.clone());\n        }\n\n        // If cwd lives inside a git repo/worktree, check whether the root git project\n        // (the primary repository working directory) is trusted. This lets\n        // worktrees inherit trust from the main project.\n        if let Some(repo_root) = resolve_root_git_project_for_trust(resolved_cwd)\n            &amp;&amp; let Some(project_config_for_root) =\n                projects.get(&amp;repo_root.to_string_lossy().to_string_lossy().to_string())\n        {\n            return Some(project_config_for_root.clone());\n        }\n\n        None\n    }\n\n    pub fn get_config_profile(\n        &amp;self,\n        override_profile: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;ConfigProfile, std::io::Error&gt; {\n        let profile = override_profile.or_else(|| self.profile.clone());\n\n        match profile {\n            Some(key) =&gt; {\n                if let Some(profile) = self.profiles.get(key.as_str()) {\n profile &#96;{key}&#96; not found\"),\n                ))\n            }\n            None =&gt; Ok(ConfigProfile::default()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Optional overrides for user configuration base_instructions,\n            developer_instructions,\n            compact_prompt,\n            include_apply_patch_tool: include_apply_patch_tool_override,\n            show_raw_agent_reasoning,\n            tools_web_search_request: override_tools_web_search_request,\n            additional_writable_roots,\n            development_mode: _development_mode_override,\n        } = overrides;\n\n        let active_profile_name = config_profile_key\n            .as_ref()\n            .or(cfg.profile.as_ref())\n            .cloned();\n        let config_profile = match active_profile_name.as_ref() {\n            Some(key) =&gt; cfg\n                .profiles\n                .get(key)\n                .ok_or_else(|| {\n                    std::io::Error::new(\n                        std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound,\n                        format!(\"config profile &#96;{key}&#96; not found\"),\n                    )\n                })?\n                .clone(),\n            None =&gt; ConfigProfile::default(),\n        };\n\n        let feature_overrides = FeatureOverrides {\n            include_apply_patch_tool: include_apply_patch_tool_override,\n            web_search_request: override_tools_web_search_request,\n        };\n\n        let features = Features::from_config(&amp;cfg, &amp;config_profile, feature_overrides);\n        #[cfg(target_os = \"windows\")]\n        {\n            crate::safety::set_windows_sandbox_enabled(features.enabled(Feature::WindowsSandbox));\n        }\n\n        let resolved_cwd = {\n            use std::env;\n\n Some(p) if p.is_absolute() =&gt; p,\n                Some(p) =&gt; {\n                    // Resolve relative path against the current working directory.\n                    tracing::info!(\"cwd is relative, resolving against current dir\");\n                    let mut current = env::current_dir()?;\n                    current.push(p);\n                    current\n                }\n model = model\n            .or(config_profile.model)\n            .or(cfg.model)\n            .unwrap_or_else(default_model);\n\n        let mut model_family =\n            find_family_for_model(&amp;model).unwrap_or_else(|| derive_default_model_family(&amp;model));\n\n        if let Some(supports_reasoning_summaries) = cfg.model_supports_reasoning_summaries {\n            model_family.supports_reasoning_summaries = supports_reasoning_summaries;\n        }\n        if let Some(model_reasoning_summary_format) = cfg.model_reasoning_summary_format {\n            model_family.reasoning_summary_format = model_reasoning_summary_format;\n        }\n\n        let openai_model_info = get_model_info(&amp;model_family);\n        let model_context_window = cfg\n compact_prompt = compact_prompt.or(cfg.compact_prompt).and_then(|value| {\n            let trimmed = value.trim();\n            if trimmed.is_empty() {\n                None\n            } else {\n -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; {\n        let base = codex_dir?;\n        for candidate in [LOCAL_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME, DEFAULT_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME] {\n            let mut path = base.to_path_buf();\n use serde::Serialize;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::shell_snapshot::ShellSnapshot;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum ShellType {
    Zsh,
    Bash,
    Sh,
    PowerShell,
    Cmd,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Shell {
    pub(crate) shell_type: ShellType,
    pub(crate) shell_path: PathBuf,
    #[serde(skip_serializing, skip_deserializing, default)]
    pub(crate) shell_snapshot: Option<Arc<ShellSnapshot>>,
}

impl Shell {
    pub fn name(&self) -> String {
        self.shell_path
            .file_name()
            .and_then(|s| s.to_str())
            .map(ToString::to_string)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("{shell_type:?}", shell_type = self.shell_type))
    }

    pub fn derive_exec_args(&self, command: &str, use_login_shell: bool) -> Vec<String> {
        let shell_path = self.shell_path.to_string_lossy().to_string();
        match self.shell_type {
            ShellType::Zsh | ShellType::Bash | ShellType::Sh => {
                let flag = if use_login_shell { "-lc" } else { "-c" };
                vec![shell_path, flag.to_string(), command.to_string()]
            }
            ShellType::PowerShell => {
                if use_login_shell {
                    vec![shell_path, "-Command".to_string(), command.to_string()]
                } else {
                    vec![
                        shell_path,
                        "-NoProfile".to_string(),
                        "-Command".to_string(),
                        command.to_string(),
                    ]
                }
            }
            ShellType::Cmd => vec![shell_path, "/C".to_string(), command.to_string()],
        }
    }
}

fn file_exists(path: &PathBuf) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    std::fs::metadata(path)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|metadata| metadata.is_file().then_some(path.clone()))
}

fn which_first(candidates: &[&str]) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    for name in candidates {
        if let Ok(path) = which::which(name) {
            return Some(path);
        }
    }
    None
}

fn shell_from_path(shell_type: ShellType, shell_path: PathBuf) -> Shell {
    Shell {
        shell_type,
        shell_path,
        shell_snapshot: None,
    }
}

fn resolve_shell_path(shell_type: ShellType, provided_path: Option<&PathBuf>) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    if let Some(path) = provided_path {
        if let Some(found) = file_exists(path) {
            return Some(found);
        }
    }

    match shell_type {
        ShellType::Zsh => which_first(&["zsh", "/bin/zsh", "/usr/bin/zsh"]),
        ShellType::Bash => which_first(&["bash", "/bin/bash", "/usr/bin/bash", "/usr/local/bin/bash"]),
        ShellType::Sh => which_first(&["sh", "/bin/sh", "/usr/bin/sh"]),
        ShellType::PowerShell => which_first(&["pwsh.exe", "pwsh", "powershell.exe", "powershell"]),
        ShellType::Cmd => which_first(&["cmd.exe", "cmd"]),
    }
}

fn ultimate_fallback_shell() -> Shell {
    if cfg!(windows) {
        shell_from_path(ShellType::Cmd, PathBuf::from("cmd.exe"))
    } else {
        shell_from_path(ShellType::Sh, PathBuf::from("/bin/sh"))
    }
}

pub fn get_shell_by_model_provided_path(shell_path: &PathBuf) -> Shell {
    detect_shell_type(shell_path)
        .and_then(|shell_type| get_shell(shell_type, Some(shell_path)))
        .unwrap_or_else(ultimate_fallback_shell)
}

pub fn get_shell(shell_type: ShellType, path: Option<&PathBuf>) -> Option<Shell> {
    resolve_shell_path(shell_type, path).map(|shell_path| shell_from_path(shell_type, shell_path))
}

pub fn detect_shell_type(shell_path: &PathBuf) -> Option<ShellType> {
    let stem = shell_path.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str())?;
    let stem = stem.to_ascii_lowercase();
    match stem.as_str() {
        "zsh" => Some(ShellType::Zsh),
        "bash" => Some(ShellType::Bash),
        "sh" => Some(ShellType::Sh),
        "pwsh" | "powershell" => Some(ShellType::PowerShell),
        "cmd" => Some(ShellType::Cmd),
        _ => None,
    }
}

#[cfg(unix)]
pub async fn default_user_shell() -> Shell {
    // Prefer $SHELL when it points to a known shell.
    if let Ok(shell) = std::env::var("SHELL") {
        let path = PathBuf::from(shell);
        if let Some(shell_type) = detect_shell_type(&path) {
            if let Some(shell) = get_shell(shell_type, Some(&path)) {
                return shell;
            }
        }
    }

    // Fallback order: zsh -> bash -> sh.
    get_shell(ShellType::Zsh, None)
        .or_else(|| get_shell(ShellType::Bash, None))
        .or_else(|| get_shell(ShellType::Sh, None))
        .unwrap_or_else(ultimate_fallback_shell)
}

#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
pub async fn default_user_shell() -> Shell {
    // Prefer PowerShell 7+ (pwsh) if present.
    if let Some(path) = which_first(&["pwsh.exe", "pwsh"]) {
        return shell_from_path(ShellType::PowerShell, path);
    }
    if let Some(path) = which_first(&["powershell.exe", "powershell"]) {
        return shell_from_path(ShellType::PowerShell, path);
    }
    // Final fallback.
    ultimate_fallback_shell()
}

#[cfg(all(not(target_os = "windows"), not(unix)))]
pub async fn default_user_shell() -> Shell {
    ultimate_fallback_shell()
}

CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED_ENV_VAR.to_string(),\n                \"1\".to_string(),\n            );\n        }\n\n        let mut command = Vec::with_capacity(1 + spec.args.len());\n        command.push(spec.program.clone());\n        command.extend(spec.args.iter().cloned());\n\n        let (command, sandbox_env, arg0_override) = match sandbox {\n            SandboxType::None =&gt; (command, HashMap::new(), None),\n            #[cfg(target_os = \"macos\")]\n            SandboxType::MacosSeatbelt =&gt; {\n                let mut seatbelt_env = HashMap::new();\n                seatbelt_env.insert(CODEX_SANDBOX_ENV_VAR.to_string(), \"seatbelt\".to_string());\n                let mut args =\n                    create_seatbelt_command_args(command.clone(), policy, sandbox_policy_cwd);\n                let mut full_command = Vec::with_capacity(1 + args.len());\n                full_command.push(MACOS_PATH_TO_SEATBELT_EXECUTABLE.to_string());\n                full_command.append(&amp;mut args);\n                (full_command, seatbelt_env, None)\n            }\n            #[cfg(not(target_os = \"macos\"))]\n            SandboxType::MacosSeatbelt =&gt; return Err(SandboxTransformError::SeatbeltUnavailable),\n            SandboxType::LinuxSeccomp =&gt; {\n                let exe = codex_linux_sandbox_exe\n                    .ok_or(SandboxTransformError::MissingLinuxSandboxExecutable)?;\n                let mut args =\n                    create_linux_sandbox_command_args(command.clone(), policy, sandbox_policy_cwd);\n                let mut full_command = Vec::with_capacity(1 + args.len());\n                full_command.push(exe.to_string_lossy().to_string());\n                full_command.append(&amp;mut args);\n                (\n                    full_command,\n                    HashMap::new(),\n                    Some(\"codex-linux-sandbox\".to_string()),\n                )\n            }\n            // On Windows, the restricted token sandbox executes in-process via the\n            // codex-windows-sandbox crate. We leave the command unchanged here and\n            // branch during execution based on the sandbox type.\n            #[cfg(target_os = \"windows\")]\n            SandboxType::WindowsRestrictedToken =&gt; (command, HashMap::new(), None),\n            // When building for non-Windows targets, this variant is never constructed.\n            #[cfg(not(target_os = \"windows\"))]\n            SandboxType::WindowsRestrictedToken =&gt; (command, HashMap::new(), None),\n        };\n\n        env.extend(sandbox_env);\n\n        Ok(ExecEnv {\n            command,\n            cwd: spec.cwd.clone(),\n            env,\n            timeout_ms: spec.timeout_ms,\n            sandbox,\n            sandbox_permissions: spec.sandbox_permissions,\n            justification: spec.justification.clone(),\n            arg0: arg0_override,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn denied(&amp;self, sandbox: SandboxType, out: &amp;ExecToolCallOutput) -&gt; bool {\n        crate::exec::is_likely_sandbox_denied(sandbox, out)\n    }\n}\n\npub async fn execute_env(\n    env: &amp;ExecEnv,\n    policy: &amp;SandboxPolicy,\n    stdout_stream: Option&lt;StdoutStream&gt;,\n) -&gt; crate::error::Result&lt;ExecToolCallOutput&gt; {\n    execute_exec_env(env.clone(), policy, stdout_stream).await\n}\n"

We do **not** walk past the Git root.\n\nuse crate::config::Config;\nuse crate::features::Feature;\nuse crate::skills::SkillMetadata;\nuse crate::skills::render_skills_section;\nuse dunce::canonicalize as normalize_path;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse tokio::io::AsyncReadExt;\nuse tracing::error;\n\n/// Default filename scanned for project-level docs.\npub const DEFAULT_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME: &amp;str = \"AGENTS.md\";\n/// Preferred local override for project-level docs.\npub const LOCAL_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME: &amp;str = \"AGENTS.override.md\";\n\n/// When both &#96;Config::instructions&#96; docs,\n        Err(e) =&gt; {\n            error!(\"error trying to find project doc: {e:#}\");\n            None\n        }\n    };\n\n    let mut out: Option&lt;String&gt; = config.user_instructions.clone();\n\n    if let Some(project_doc) = project_docs {\n        out = match out {\n            Some(existing) =&gt; Some(format!(\"{existing}{PROJECT_DOC_SEPARATOR}{project_doc}\")),\n            None =&gt; Some(project_doc),\n        };\n    }\n\n    if let Some(skills_section) = skills_section {\n        out = match out {\n            Some(existing) =&gt; Some(format!(\"{existing}\\n\\n{skills_section}\")),\n            None =&gt; Some(skills_section),\n        };\n    }\n\n    out\n}\n\n/// Extract language setting from AGENTS.md content\n///\n/// Supports patterns like:\n/// - &#96;language: ja&#96;\n/// - &#96;- language: en&#96;\n/// - &#96;Language: zh&#96;\npub fn extract_language_setting(content: &amp;str) -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; {\n    use regex::Regex;\n\n    // Pattern 1: \"- language: ja\" (list format)\n    // Pattern 2: \"language: en\" (key-value format)\n    let patterns = [\n        r\"(?mi)^-?\\s*language:\\s*(\\w+)\",\n        r\"(?mi)^-?\\s*review_language:\\s*(\\w+)\",\n    ];\n\n    for pattern_str in &amp;patterns {\n        if let Ok(re) = Regex::new(pattern_str) {\n            if let Some(captures) = re.captures(content) {\n                if let Some(lang_match) = captures.get(1) {\n                    let lang = lang_match.as_str().to_lowercase();\n                    tracing::debug!(\"Extracted language setting: {}\", lang);\n                    return Some(lang);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    None\n}\n\n/// Get language setting from project documentation\npub async fn get_language_setting(config: &amp;Config) -&gt; Unexpected I/O failures bubble up as &#96;Err&#96; so\n/// callers can decide how to handle them.\npub async fn read_project_docs(config: &amp;Config) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;Option&lt;String&gt;&gt; {\n    let max_total = config.project_doc_max_bytes;\n\n    if max_total == 0 {\n        return Ok(None);\n    }\n\n    let paths = discover_project_doc_paths(config)?;\n    if paths.is_empty() {\n        return Ok(None);\n    }\n\n    let mut remaining: u64 = max_total as u64;\n    let mut parts: Vec&lt;String&gt; = Vec::new();\n\n    for p in paths {\n        if remaining == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n\n        let file = match tokio::fs::File::open(&amp;p).await {\n            Ok(f) =&gt; f,\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound =&gt; continue,\n            Err(e) =&gt; return Err(e),\n        };\n\n        let size = file.metadata().await?.len();\n        let mut reader = tokio::io::BufReader::new(file).take(remaining);\n        let mut data: Vec&lt;u8&gt; = Vec::new();\n        reader.read_to_end(&amp;mut data).await?;\n\n        if size &gt; remaining {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                \"Project doc &#96;{}&#96; exceeds remaining budget ({} bytes) - truncating.\",\n                p.display(),\n                remaining,\n            );\n        }\n\n        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&amp;data).to_string();\n        if !text.trim().is_empty() {\n            parts.push(text);\n            remaining = remaining.saturating_sub(data.len() as u64);\n        }\n    }\n\n    if parts.is_empty() {\n        Ok(None)\n    } else {\n        Ok(Some(parts.join(\"\\n\\n\")))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Discover the list of AGENTS.md files using the same search rules as\n/// &#96;read_project_docs&#96;, but return the file paths instead of concatenated\n/// contents. sections = Vec::new();\r\n\r\n    if !response.chunk_id.is_empty() {\r\n        sections.push(format!(\"Chunk ID: {}\", response.chunk_id));\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    let wall_time_seconds = response.wall_time.as_secs_f64();\r\n    sections.push(format!(\"Wall time: {wall_time_seconds:.4} seconds\"));\r\n\r\n    if let Some(exit_code) = response.exit_code {\r\n        sections.push(format!(\"Process exited with code {exit_code}\"));\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    if let Some(process_id) = response.process_id.as_ref() {\r\n        sections.push(format!(\"Process running with id {process_id}\"));\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    if let Some(original_token_count) = response.original_token_count {\r\n        sections.push(format!(\"Original token count: {original_token_count}\"));\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    sections.push(\"Output:\".to_string());\r\n    sections.push(response.output.clone());\r\n\r\n    sections.join(\"\\n\")\r\n}\r\n\r\n\r\n"
}

Must be 1 or greater.\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"limit\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\"The maximum number of lines to return.\".to_string()),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"mode\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::String {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Optional mode selector: \\\"slice\\\" for simple ranges (default) or \\\"indentation\\\" \\\n                 to expand around an anchor line.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n\n    let mut indentation_properties = BTreeMap::new();\n    indentation_properties.insert(\n        \"anchor_line\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Anchor line to center the indentation lookup on (defaults to offset).\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    indentation_properties.insert(\n        \"max_levels\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\n                \"How many parent indentation levels (smaller indents) to include.\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    indentation_properties.insert(\n        \"include_siblings\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Boolean {\n            description: Some(\n                \"When true, include additional blocks that share the anchor indentation.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    indentation_properties.insert(\n        \"include_header\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Boolean {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Include doc comments or attributes directly above the selected block.\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    indentation_properties.insert(\n        \"max_lines\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Hard cap on the number of lines returned when using indentation mode.\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"indentation\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Object {\n            properties: indentation_properties,\n            required: None,\n            additional_properties: Some(false.into()),\n        },\n    );\n\n    ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool {\n        name: \"read_file\".to_string(),\n        description:\n            \"Reads a local file with 1-indexed line numbers, supporting slice and indentation-aware block modes.\"\n                .to_string(),\n        strict: false,\n        parameters: JsonSchema::Object {\n            properties,\n            required: Some(vec![\"file_path\".to_string()]),\n            additional_properties: Some(false.into()),\n        },\n    })\n}\n\npub(crate) fn create_list_dir_tool() -&gt; ToolSpec {\n    let mut properties = BTreeMap::new();\n    properties.insert(\n        \"dir_path\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::String {\n            description: Some(\"Absolute path to the directory to list.\".to_string()),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n Must be 1 or greater.\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"limit\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\"The maximum number of entries to return.\".to_string()),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"depth\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\n                \"The maximum directory depth to traverse. Must be 1 or greater.\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n\n    ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool {\n        name: \"list_dir\".to_string(),\n        description:\n            \"Lists entries in a local directory with 1-indexed entry numbers and simple type labels.\"\n                .to_string(),\n        strict: false,\n        parameters: JsonSchema::Object {\n            properties,\n            required: Some(vec![\"dir_path\".to_string()]),\n            additional_properties: Some(false.into()),\n        },\n    })\n}\n\nfn create_list_mcp_resources_tool() -&gt; ToolSpec {\n    let mut properties = BTreeMap::new();\n    properties.insert(\n        \"server\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::String {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Optional MCP server name. When omitted, lists resources from every configured server.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"cursor\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::String {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Opaque cursor returned by a previous list_mcp_resources call for the same server.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n\n    ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool {\n        name: \"list_mcp_resources\".to_string(),\n        description: \"Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"uri\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::String {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n\n    ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool {\n        name: \"read_mcp_resource\".to_string(),\n        description:\n            \"Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.\"\n                .to_string(),\n        strict: false,\n        parameters: JsonSchema::Object {\n            properties,\n            required: Some(vec![\"server\".to_string(), \"uri\".to_string()]),\n            additional_properties: Some(false.into()),\n        },\n    })\n}\n/// TODO(dylan): deprecate once we get rid of json tool\n#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub(crate) struct ApplyPatchToolArgs {\n    pub(crate) input: String,\n}\n\n/// Returns JSON values that are compatible with Function Calling in the\n/// Responses API:\n/// https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling?api-mode=responses\npub fn create_tools_json_for_responses_api(\n    tools: &amp;[ToolSpec],\n) -&gt; crate::error::Result&lt;Vec&lt;serde_json::Value&gt;&gt; {\n    let mut tools_json = Vec::new();\n\n    for tool in tools {\n        let json = serde_json::to_value(tool)?;\n        tools_json.push(json);\n    }\n\n    Ok(tools_json)\n}\n/// Returns JSON values that are compatible with Function Calling in the\n/// Chat Completions API:\n/// https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling?api-mode=chat\npub(crate) fn create_tools_json_for_chat_completions_api(\n    tools: &amp;[ToolSpec],\n) -&gt; crate::error::Result&lt;Vec&lt;serde_json::Value&gt;&gt; {\n    // We start with the JSON for the Responses API and than rewrite it to match\n    // the chat completions tool call format.\n    let responses_api_tools_json = create_tools_json_for_responses_api(tools)?;\n    let tools_json = responses_api_tools_json\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter_map(|mut tool| {\n            if tool.get(\"type\") != Some(&amp;serde_json::Value::String(\"function\".to_string())) {\n                return None;\n            }\n\n            if let Some(map) = tool.as_object_mut() {\n                let name = map\n                    .get(\"name\")\n                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                    .unwrap_or_default()\n                    .to_string();\n                // Remove \"type\" field as it is not needed in chat completions.\n                map.remove(\"type\");\n                Some(json!({\n                    \"type\": \"function\",\n                    \"name\": name,\n                    \"function\": map,\n                }))\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .collect::&lt;Vec&lt;serde_json::Value&gt;&gt;();\n    Ok(tools_json)\n}\n\npub(crate) fn mcp_tool_to_openai_tool(\n    fully_qualified_name: String,\n    tool: mcp_types::Tool,\n) -&gt; Result&lt;ResponsesApiTool, serde_json::Error&gt; {\n    let mcp_types::Tool {\n        description,\n        mut input_schema,\n        ..\n    } = tool;\n\n    // OpenAI models mandate the \"properties\" field in the schema. The Agents\n    // SDK fixed this by inserting an empty object for \"properties\" if it is not\n    // already present https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/issues/449\n    // so here we do the same.\n    if input_schema.properties.is_none() {\n        input_schema.properties = Some(serde_json::Value::Object(serde_json::Map::new()));\n    }\n\n    // Serialize to a raw JSON value so we can sanitize schemas coming from MCP\n    // servers. Some servers omit the top-level or nested &#96;type&#96; in JSON\n    // Schemas (e.g. using enum/anyOf), or use unsupported variants like\n    // &#96;integer&#96;. Our internal JsonSchema is a small subset and requires\n    // &#96;type&#96;, so we coerce/sanitize here for compatibility.\n    let mut serialized_input_schema = serde_json::to_value(input_schema)?;\n    sanitize_json_schema(&amp;mut serialized_input_schema);\n    let input_schema = serde_json::from_value::&lt;JsonSchema&gt;(serialized_input_schema)?;\n\n    Ok(ResponsesApiTool {\n        name: fully_qualified_name,\n        description: description.unwrap_or_default(),\n        strict: false,\n        parameters: input_schema,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Sanitize a JSON Schema (as serde_json::Value) so it can fit our limited\n/// JsonSchema enum. This function:\n/// - Ensures every schema object has a \"type\". If missing, infers it from\n///   common keywords (properties =&gt; object, items =&gt; array, enum/const/format =&gt; string)\n///   and otherwise defaults to \"string\".\n/// - Fills required child fields (e.g. array items, object properties) with\n///   permissive defaults when absent.\nfn sanitize_json_schema(value: &amp;mut JsonValue) {\n    match value {\n        JsonValue::Bool(_) =&gt; {\n            // JSON Schema boolean form: true/false. Coerce to an accept-all string.\n            *value = json!({ \"type\": \"string\" });\n        }\n        JsonValue::Array(arr) =&gt; {\n            for v in arr.iter_mut() {\n                sanitize_json_schema(v);\n            }\n        }\n        JsonValue::Object(map) =&gt; {\n            // First, recursively sanitize known nested schema holders\n            if let Some(props) = map.get_mut(\"properties\")\n                &amp;&amp; let Some(props_map) = props.as_object_mut()\n            {\n                for (_k, v) in props_map.iter_mut() {\n                    sanitize_json_schema(v);\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(items) = map.get_mut(\"items\") {\n                sanitize_json_schema(items);\n            }\n            // Some schemas use oneOf/anyOf/allOf - sanitize their entries\n            for combiner in [\"oneOf\", \"anyOf\", \"allOf\", \"prefixItems\"] {\n                if let Some(v) = map.get_mut(combiner) {\n                    sanitize_json_schema(v);\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Normalize/ensure type\n            let mut ty = map.get(\"type\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(str::to_string);\n\n            // If type is an array (union), pick first supported; else leave to inference\n            if ty.is_none()\n                &amp;&amp; let Some(JsonValue::Array(types)) = map.get(\"type\")\n            {\n                for t in types {\n                    if let Some(tt) = t.as_str()\n                        &amp;&amp; matches!(\n                            tt,\n                            \"object\" | \"array\" | \"string\" | \"number\" | \"integer\" | \"boolean\"\n                        )\n                    {\n                        ty = Some(tt.to_string());\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Infer type if still missing\n            if ty.is_none() {\n                if map.contains_key(\"properties\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"required\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"additionalProperties\")\n                {\n                    ty = Some(\"object\".to_string());\n                } else if map.contains_key(\"items\") || map.contains_key(\"prefixItems\") {\n                    ty = Some(\"array\".to_string());\n                } else if map.contains_key(\"enum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"const\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"format\")\n                {\n                    ty = Some(\"string\".to_string());\n                } else if map.contains_key(\"minimum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"maximum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"exclusiveMinimum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"exclusiveMaximum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"multipleOf\")\n                {\n                    ty = Some(\"number\".to_string());\n                }\n            }\n            // If we still couldn't infer, default to string\n            let ty = ty.unwrap_or_else(|| \"string\".to_string());\n            map.insert(\"type\".to_string(), JsonValue::String(ty.to_string()));\n\n            // Ensure object schemas have properties map\n            if ty == \"object\" {\n                if !map.contains_key(\"properties\") {\n                    map.insert(\n                        \"properties\".to_string(),\n                        JsonValue::Object(serde_json::Map::new()),\n                    );\n                }\n                // If additionalProperties is an object schema, sanitize it too.\n                // Leave booleans as-is, since JSON Schema allows boolean here.\n                if let Some(ap) = map.get_mut(\"additionalProperties\") {\n                    let is_bool = matches!(ap, JsonValue::Bool(_));\n                    if !is_bool {\n                        sanitize_json_schema(ap);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Ensure array schemas have items\n            if ty == \"array\" &amp;&amp; !map.contains_key(\"items\") {\n                map.insert(\"items\".to_string(), json!({ \"type\": \"string\" }));\n            }\n        }\n        _ =&gt; {}\n    }\n}\n\n/// Builds the tool registry builder while collecting tool specs for later serialization.\npub(crate) fn build_specs(\n    config: &amp;ToolsConfig,\n    mcp_tools: Option&lt;HashMap&lt;String, mcp_types::Tool&gt;&gt;,\n) -&gt; ToolRegistryBuilder {\n    use crate::tools::handlers::ApplyPatchHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::GrepFilesHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::ListDirHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::McpHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::McpResourceHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::PlanHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::ReadFileHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::ShellHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::TestSyncHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::UnifiedExecHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::ViewImageHandler;\n    use std::sync::Arc;\n\n    let mut builder = ToolRegistryBuilder::new();\n\n    let shell_handler = Arc::new(ShellHandler);\n    let unified_exec_handler = Arc::new(UnifiedExecHandler);\n    let plan_handler = Arc::new(PlanHandler);\n    let apply_patch_handler = Arc::new(ApplyPatchHandler);\n    let view_image_handler = Arc::new(ViewImageHandler);\n    let mcp_handler = Arc::new(McpHandler);\n    let mcp_resource_handler = Arc::new(McpResourceHandler);\n\n    match &amp;config.shell_type {\n        ConfigShellToolType::Default =&gt; {\n            builder.push_spec(create_shell_tool());\n        }\n        ConfigShellToolType::Local =&gt; {\n            builder.push_spec(ToolSpec::LocalShell {});\n        }\n        ConfigShellToolType::UnifiedExec =&gt; {\n            builder.push_spec(create_exec_command_tool());\n            builder.push_spec(create_write_stdin_tool());\n            builder.register_handler(\"exec_command\", unified_exec_handler.clone());\n            builder.register_handler(\"write_stdin\", unified_exec_handler);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Always register shell aliases so older prompts remain compatible.\n    builder.register_handler(\"shell\", shell_handler.clone());\n    builder.register_handler(\"container.exec\", shell_handler.clone());\n    builder.register_handler(\"local_shell\", shell_handler);\n\n    builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_list_mcp_resources_tool(), true);\n    builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_list_mcp_resource_templates_tool(), true);\n    builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_read_mcp_resource_tool(), true);\n    builder.register_handler(\"list_mcp_resources\", mcp_resource_handler.clone());\n    builder.register_handler(\"list_mcp_resource_templates\", mcp_resource_handler.clone());\n    builder.register_handler(\"read_mcp_resource\", mcp_resource_handler);\n\n    builder.push_spec(PLAN_TOOL.clone());\n    builder.register_handler(\"update_plan\", plan_handler);\n\n    if let Some(apply_patch_tool_type) = &amp;config.apply_patch_tool_type {\n        match apply_patch_tool_type {\n            ApplyPatchToolType::Freeform =&gt; {\n                builder.push_spec(create_apply_patch_freeform_tool());\n            }\n            ApplyPatchToolType::Function =&gt; {\n                builder.push_spec(create_apply_patch_json_tool());\n            }\n        }\n        builder.register_handler(\"apply_patch\", apply_patch_handler);\n    }\n\n    if config\n        .experimental_supported_tools\n        .contains(&amp;\"grep_files\".to_string())\n    {\n        let grep_files_handler = Arc::new(GrepFilesHandler);\n        builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_grep_files_tool(), true);\n        builder.register_handler(\"grep_files\", grep_files_handler);\n    }\n\n    if config\n        .experimental_supported_tools\n        .contains(&amp;\"read_file\".to_string())\n    {\n        let read_file_handler = Arc::new(ReadFileHandler);\n        builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_read_file_tool(), true);\n        builder.register_handler(\"read_file\", read_file_handler);\n    }\n\n    if config\n        .experimental_supported_tools\n        .iter()\n        .any(|tool| tool == \"list_dir\")\n    {\n        let list_dir_handler = Arc::new(ListDirHandler);\n        builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_list_dir_tool(), true);\n        builder.register_handler(\"list_dir\", list_dir_handler);\n    }\n\n    if config\n        .experimental_supported_tools\n        .contains(&amp;\"test_sync_tool\".to_string())\n    {\n        let test_sync_handler = Arc::new(TestSyncHandler);\n        builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_test_sync_tool(), true);\n        builder.register_handler(\"test_sync_tool\", test_sync_handler);\n    }\n\n    if config.web_search_request {\n        builder.push_spec(ToolSpec::WebSearch {});\n    }\n\n    // Deep web search is now handled by MCP server\n    // if config.deep_web_search {\n    //     let deep_web_search_handler = Arc::new(crate::tools::handlers::DeepWebSearchHandler);\n    //     builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(\n    //         ToolSpec::Function(crate::tools::handlers::create_deep_web_search_tool()),\n    //         false, // Deep research is async and may take time\n    //     );\n    //     builder.register_handler(\"deep_web_search\", deep_web_search_handler);\n    // }\n\n    if config.include_view_image_tool {\n        builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_view_image_tool(), true);\n        builder.register_handler(\"view_image\", view_image_handler);\n    }\n\n    if let Some(mcp_tools) = mcp_tools {\n        let mut entries: Vec&lt;(String, mcp_types::Tool)&gt; = mcp_tools.into_iter().collect();\n        entries.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&amp;b.0));\n\n        for (name, tool) in entries.into_iter() {\n            match mcp_tool_to_openai_tool(name.clone(), tool.clone()) {\n                Ok(converted_tool) =&gt; {\n                    builder.push_spec(ToolSpec::Function(converted_tool));\n                    builder.register_handler(name, mcp_handler.clone());\n                }\n                Err(e) =&gt; {\n                    tracing::error!(\"Failed to convert {name:?} MCP tool to OpenAI tool: {e:?}\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    builder\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use crate::client_common::tools::FreeformTool;\n    use crate::model_family::find_family_for_model;\n    use crate::tools::registry::ConfiguredToolSpec;\n    use mcp_types::ToolInputSchema;\n    use pretty_assertions::assert_eq;\n\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn tool_name(tool: &amp;ToolSpec) -&gt; &amp;str {\n        match tool {\n            ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool { name, .. }) =&gt; name,\n            ToolSpec::LocalShell {} =&gt; \"local_shell\",\n            ToolSpec::WebSearch {} =&gt; \"web_search\",\n            ToolSpec::Freeform(FreeformTool { name, .. }) =&gt; name,\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Avoid order-based assertions; compare via set containment instead.\n    fn assert_contains_tool_names(tools: &amp;[ConfiguredToolSpec], expected_subset: &amp;[&amp;str]) {\n        use std::collections::HashSet;\n        let mut names = HashSet::new();\n        let mut duplicates = Vec::new();\n        for name in tools.iter().map(|t| tool_name(&amp;t.spec)) {\n            if !names.insert(name) {\n                duplicates.push(name);\n            }\n        }\n        assert!(\n            duplicates.is_empty(),\n            \"duplicate tool entries detected: {duplicates:?}\"\n        );\n        for expected in expected_subset {\n            assert!(\n                names.contains(expected),\n                \"expected tool {expected} to be present; had: {names:?}\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn shell_tool_name(config: &amp;ToolsConfig) -&gt; Option&lt;&amp;'static str&gt; {\n        match config.shell_type {\n            ConfigShellToolType::Default =&gt; Some(\"shell\"),\n            ConfigShellToolType::Local =&gt; Some(\"local_shell\"),\n            ConfigShellToolType::UnifiedExec =&gt; None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn find_tool&lt;'a&gt;(\n        tools: &amp;'a [ConfiguredToolSpec],\n        expected_name: &amp;str,\n    ) -&gt; &amp;'a ConfiguredToolSpec {\n        tools\n            .iter()\n            .find(|tool| tool_name(&amp;tool.spec) == expected_name)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!(\"expected tool {expected_name}\"))\n    }\n\n    fn strip_descriptions_schema(schema: &amp;mut JsonSchema) {\n        match schema {\n            JsonSchema::Boolean { description }\n description } =&gt; {\n                strip_descriptions_schema(items);\n                *description = None;\n            }\n            JsonSchema::Object {\n                properties,\n                required: _,\n                additional_properties,\n            } =&gt; {\n                for v in properties.values_mut() {\n                    strip_descriptions_schema(v);\n                }\n                if let Some(AdditionalProperties::Schema(s)) = additional_properties {\n                    strip_descriptions_schema(s);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn strip_descriptions_tool(spec: &amp;mut ToolSpec) {\n        match spec {\n            ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool { parameters, .. }) =&gt; {\n test_full_toolset_specs_for_gpt5_codex_unified_exec_web_search() {\n        let model_family = find_family_for_model(\"gpt-5-codex\")\n            .expect(\"gpt-5-codex should be a valid model family\");\n        let mut features = Features::with_defaults();\n        features.enable(Feature::UnifiedExec);\n        features.enable(Feature::WebSearchRequest);\n        features.enable(Feature::ViewImageTool);\n        let config = ToolsConfig::new(&amp;ToolsConfigParams {\n            model_family: &amp;model_family,\n            features: &amp;features,\n        });\n        let (tools, _) = build_specs(&amp;config, None).build();\n\n        // Build actual map name -&gt; spec\n        use std::collections::BTreeMap;\n        use std::collections::HashSet;\n
